advances: The all-active-normal pointwise formula strengthens the almost-everywhere boundary formula. No depth payment is deduced.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
Apply 84cd8a85417b0d7a with one singleton ceiling $h_L$ and field $\Psi$. Its inner homothet proof gives the uniform $O(\varepsilon)$ bound and hence $x_\varepsilon\to x$. For each old active $n$ the defining inequality gives $s_\varepsilon h_L(n)\ge\varepsilon\Psi(n,x_\varepsilon)$. The lower limit therefore dominates the maximum over the compact active set.

If the upper limit is positive, take a sequence realizing it with $s_\varepsilon>0$. The endpoint is then interior to the old $L$. Some defining cut at $n_\varepsilon$ is tight, because a strict slack at every cut would give positive minimum slack on the compact unit sphere and let the ray advance. Pass to a subsequence with $n_\varepsilon\to n_*$. The equality reads
$$
h_L(n_\varepsilon)-n_\varepsilon\cdot x+s_\varepsilon n_\varepsilon\cdot x
=\varepsilon\Psi(n_\varepsilon,x_\varepsilon).
$$
The old support gap tends to zero, so $n_*$ supports $L$ at $x$ and $n_\varepsilon\cdot x\to h_L(n_*)>0$. Dropping the nonnegative gap and dividing gives upper limit at most $\Psi(n_*,x)/h_L(n_*)$. If the upper limit is zero the lower bound already gives equality. This establishes the formula without choosing a single normal at a corner.
statement:
Let $L\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge1$, be a convex body with $0$ interior, and let $\Psi(n,x)$ be nonnegative and jointly continuous on the unit sphere times a neighborhood of $L$, convex in $x$ for each $n$. Erode $L$ by imposing $n\cdot x+\varepsilon\Psi(n,x)\le h_L(n)$ for all unit $n$ on $L$. For every old boundary point $x$ write the new endpoint on its ray as $x_\varepsilon=(1-s_\varepsilon)x$. Then
$$
\lim_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}\frac{s_\varepsilon}{\varepsilon}
=\max_{n\in N_L(x)}\frac{\Psi(n,x)}{h_L(n)},
$$
where $N_L(x)$ is the set of unit outward supporting normals at $x$. The fractional radial loss is uniformly $O(\varepsilon)$ on the whole boundary.
title: Radial loss at every boundary point of a support erosion
